drafted_from: tool:search-freesound-for-free-sound-effects row in tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/ and tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/test/test_judge_sound_effects.py (run for real on made-up tones)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Search Freesound for CC0 and CC BY soft tick sounds under one second and write /work/sfx/fs-candidates.json." It runs the Freesound search and tells you how many it found per category.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads a queries.json on this computer, reads Freesound's public search pages and writes a candidates.json file.
instructions: 1. Write /work/sfx/fs-queries.json: {"tick": {"queries": ["soft tick"], "max_s": 1.0}} (category, its search words, the longest length in seconds; min_s is optional).

2. Say "Search Freesound". The AI reads the row with tools:list and runs: python3 -I tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/search_freesound.py /work/sfx/fs-queries.json /work/sfx/fs-candidates.json (it needs the internet and waits 1.5 s between requests).
3. Read the last line (count per category), then open fs-candidates.json for each item's id, user, title, duration, downloads, page and preview address.
4. Choose items and pass them to tool:fetch-free-sound-effects-with-their-licences, which reads each licence before it downloads.

worked_examples.title: One soft tick found, listed once although the page shows it twice
worked_examples.ask: Search Freesound for a soft tick under one second.
worked_examples.given: From tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/test/test_judge_sound_effects.py (test_freesound_and_mixkit_searches_keep_each_item_once_within_its_length, made-up Freesound page): fs-queries.json is {"tick": {"queries": ["soft tick"], "max_s": 1.0}}. Command: python3 -I tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/search_freesound.py /work/sfx/fs-queries.json /work/sfx/fs-candidates.json. It reads two pages (one per licence filter, Creative Commons 0 and Attribution), each with duration filter [0 TO 1.0].
